candidates.buyer: Village Water Boards (about 117 rural systems, seven-member boards chaired by the village council chair), plus the Ministry of Rural Transformation's rural water unit
candidates.category: 13. Small water systems
candidates.existing: No billing product for village boards found; donor programmes deliver training and meters, not software. Not confirmed that none exists.
candidates.name: Village Water Board billing, collections and monthly-accounts pack
candidates.trigger: Village Councils Act Cap. 88 s.43A: boards keep records and accounts, collect user fees and run disconnections. S.I. 190 of 2004 requires monthly financial reports to the Ministry. Flat-rate billing, low collection and high delinquency (CARICOM Development Fund); IDB micro-metering pilot and BSIF board-capacity programmes are under way; a rural water policy is being drafted.
candidates.unchecked: Competitor search (water board billing software) not run, budget. Whether boards own PCs, who pays (boards are poor, so likely donor or Ministry-funded), and whether the Ministry mandates a template. Procurement is donor-led, so a sale would be to the Ministry or IDB, not to the boards.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: No Belize law licensing gold jewellery dealers surfaced. Exchange Control Regulations (Cap. 52) have a Part I on dealings in gold and foreign currency; contents not confirmed. Pawnbroking (which takes gold) is licensed by the Central Bank as Registrar under the Moneylenders Act and Moneylenders Regulations 2017 (see candidate C-BZ-03).

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: One search returned only foreign law. No Belize dismantler licence or end-of-life vehicle rule found. Nothing to build on; the Transport Department and Department of the Environment were not checked directly.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K05. Cattle movement permits are issued at BAHA offices (Orange Walk, Belize City, Central Farm) under S.I. 77 of 2011 (Animal Identification), with a Belize Livestock Registry run by BLPA under an MOU with BAHA and OIRSA. No 2025-26 evidence of a digital movement permit. Slaughter of Animals Act (Cap. 154) requires a Minister's slaughterer licence and a licensed slaughterhouse for export animals.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Bees Control Act (Cap. 206) requires registration of apiary owners and apiaries and notification of foulbrood, Nosema and other disease to the Chief Agricultural Officer and BAHA. Ministry page says honey is consumed locally with no exports, though a minister has said exports may resume (sources conflict). Pool is small and the duty light. Nothing worth a candidate.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: National Integrated Water Resources Act (Cap. 222:01): water abstraction licence needed, well drillers must be licensed (s.41), licence register kept. National Hydrological Service issues Permission to Drill and abstraction licences, needs a BWS No Objection letter inside BWS areas, and a DOE effluent clearance if wastewater is discharged. Weak candidate C-BZ-05.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: DOE requires Environmental Clearance (2019 press release) for anyone collecting sewage from homes or businesses, with disposal only at approved sites. DOE effluent licences renew each 1 April (fee $500 in 2020/21). Candidate C-BZ-04 (weak, small pool).

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: One search found no Belize elevator, boiler or pressure-vessel inspection law; results were all foreign. Not confirmed either way; Labour Act and Cap. 297 subsidiary laws not checked.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: About 117 rural water systems serving about 132 villages (undated government presentation) run by Village Water Boards under Village Councils Act s.43A. Duties: keep records, collect user fees, monthly financial reports to the Ministry (S.I. 190 of 2004). Flat-rate billing, low collection and delinquency; IDB and BSIF programmes are building board capacity and piloting micro-metering. PUC licence covers BWS, not village boards. Candidate C-BZ-01.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Labour Act Cap. 297 s.68 requires recruiters to be licensed; Labour (Recruiting of Workers) Regulations require an application to the Commissioner, a bond, a register and accounts (2003 edition; current fees and forms not found). Botswana pages in the results are not Belize and were ignored. Pool probably very small. Candidate C-BZ-06 (unverified).

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Burial on private land needs permission of the Director of Health Services under Public Health Act Cap. 40 s.31 (BZ$1,000 fine for breach); cemeteries are partly run by city councils. No funeral-home licensing regime found. Nothing worth a candidate.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Cambio licensing (Exchange Control Regs Part IX) was repealed in July 2005 and cambios closed; border cambiadores operated informally. Vendors need municipal trade licences: Belmopan council pressed market-plaza vendors for individual licences (2025) after a disputed blanket MOU. Trade Licensing Act 2024 (Act 19 of 2024) is not yet in force (Dec 2025 press release); Cap. 66 still applies, and renewal under the new Act is due 15 November. The government launched the TRALMAS digital trade licence portal on 31 July (2026 per the article date). Candidate C-BZ-02 (weak, state portal covers it).

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: BAHA Food Safety Regulations 2001 (S.I. 25 of 2001): food enterprises register with BAHA and follow HACCP. Food handler permits are annual, with an exam, through Environmental Health. Daycare is regulated (minimum standards, registration), but the issuing body was not confirmed. Under the 2024 Trade Licensing Act, day care and light repair get auto-approval. No tattoo or driving-school regime found.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Grain Act (Cap. 288) covers corn, rice, beans and sorghum and defines grain processing units (rice, flour and feed mills, silos) with a Grain Commission.
